summary: A container held by the server. It can be a chest in the world, which players in view see as the game's container and open with the use key, a storage with no world object that only scripts open, such as a bank, or the searchable body of a knocked-out player or dead NPC. Only the player who opened it receives its contents.

name.summary: 'spawned_stash_<number>' for a chest a script placed, 'level_chest_<placedGuid>' for an adopted level chest, or '' for a storage.

model.summary: The model from Stash.spawn's options.model. Empty for the default chest and for level chests, whose models Stash.levelChests lists.
model.exampleLua:
local cabinet = kcds.world.Stash.spawn({ x = 1650, y = 2151, z = 35 }, {}, nil, { model = "objects/manmade/common_furniture/cabinets/cabinet_fancy_d.cgf" })
print(cabinet.model or "the default chest")
model.exampleCs:
var cabinet = Stash.Spawn(new { x = 1650, y = 2151, z = 35 }, new { }, null, new { model = "objects/manmade/common_furniture/cabinets/cabinet_fancy_d.cgf" });
Log.Info((string.IsNullOrEmpty(cabinet.Model) ? "the default chest" : cabinet.Model));

lockedAtBoot.summary: Whether the level locks it, for an adopted level chest built locked. A chest placed by a script is never built locked.
lockedAtBoot.exampleLua:
local chest = kcds.world.Stash.adopt("010c6d3de8ab0cb9")
if (chest and chest.lockedAtBoot) then
  print("the level locks this chest")
end

spawn.summary: Places a chest, or any other mesh as a container. All clients in view build it and offer the game's Search. Throws a TypeError for options that are not an object, or a model that is not a .cgf, .cga or .cdf path.

params.options: Optional: { model }, a .cgf, .cga or .cdf path of up to 255 bytes with forward slashes, such as 'objects/manmade/common_furniture/cabinets/cabinet_fancy_d.cgf'. A mesh with no open and close animations does not visibly open, and a client unable to load it shows the default chest.

spawn.exampleLua:
local chest = kcds.world.Stash.spawn(kcds.math.Vector3.new(100, 200, 10))
chest:addItem({ item = "apple", amount = 3 })
chest.locked = true
chest.canBePicked = true

getById.summary: The stash with this network id, or null.
getById.exampleLua:
kcds.core.Events.fromClient("bank:open", function(player, payload)
  local vault = kcds.world.Stash.getById(tonumber((payload and payload.id)))
  if (vault and vault.isStorage) then
    vault:open(player)
  end
end)

createStorage.summary: Creates a storage with no world object, which scripts open for players.
createStorage.exampleLua:
local bank = kcds.world.Stash.createStorage()

kcds.core.Events.on("playerCommand", function(player, command)
  if command == "bank" then
    bank:open(player)
  end
end)

playerInventory.summary: A view of a connected player's own inventory, as a storage another player opens from anywhere with open(viewer): the game's own transfer screen with everything the player carries and wears, their keyring left out. What the viewer takes leaves the player, worn things too, which their game takes off them; playerInventoryTake can refuse each take and playerInventoryTaken follows. With `put: true` the viewer can also give the player things from their own inventory (playerInventoryGive, playerInventoryGiven). Changes the player makes meanwhile show at once. Nobody opens a view of their own inventory, one viewer has it open at a time, and it goes when the player leaves or the resource stops; destroy() removes it sooner. Throws a TypeError for a player who is not connected or options that are not { put }.

params.player: The player whose inventory it shows.

playerInventory.exampleLua:
-- /inv <id>: an admin goes through a player's pockets and kit.
kcds.core.Events.on("playerCommand", function(admin, command, args)
  local target = kcds.players.Player.getById(tonumber(args[1]))
  if command == "inv" and admin.state:get("role") == "admin" and target then
    kcds.world.Stash.playerInventory(target, { put = true }):open(admin)
  end
end)

find.summary: A chest by GUID, or an adopted level chest by level GUID, in its dimension, or null.

nearest.summary: The nearest chest within maxDistance, skipping storages, or null.
nearest.exampleLua:
local chest = kcds.world.Stash.nearest(player.position, 3)
if chest then
  kcds.core.Chat.sendToPlayer(player, tostring(chest.itemCount) .. " rows in the chest")
end

levelChests.summary: The sacks, barrels, wardrobes and chests the server's level places, within `radius` metres of a position, or all of them with no position. Each is { placedGuid, position, model, lockedAtBoot, canBePicked, lockLevel }, where lockLevel is the level's, 0 to 1, or null where the game makes one up on reset. They belong to the game, with each player's game filling them as the level says, until Stash.adopt hands one to the server.
levelChests.returns: { placedGuid, position, model, lockedAtBoot, canBePicked, lockLevel }[]
levelChests.exampleLua:
for _, nearby in ipairs(kcds.world.Stash.levelChests(player.position, 5)) do
  print(nearby.placedGuid, nearby.model, (nearby.lockedAtBoot and "locked" or "open"))
end

adopt.summary: Hands a level chest to the server. It then holds what the server gives it, starting empty and dropping what the game put in. It keeps the level's lock until a script changes locked, canBePicked or keyClass, and all players open it as a server chest, with stashInteract and the server's lock and key. destroy() returns it to the game, which keeps the lock and what it last showed. Adopting the same chest again in that dimension gives the same Stash. Null if the server's level has no chest with that GUID.

params.placedGuid: The level GUID from Stash.levelChests, sixteen hex digits, with or without 0x.

adopt.exampleLua:
-- This chest opens only with its own key.
local Stash = kcds.world.Stash

local closest = table.unpack(Stash.levelChests(player.position, 3))
local keyedChest = closest and Stash.adopt(closest.placedGuid)
if keyedChest then
  keyedChest.keyClass = (kcds.players.Items.effective("key_custom") and kcds.players.Items.effective("key_custom").id) or ""
  keyedChest.canBePicked = false
  keyedChest.locked = true
end

destroyAll.summary: Removes all stashes, or those in one dimension, and returns how many. Bodies of players and NPCs stay.

params.dimension: Optional: limits it to this dimension.

placedGuid.summary: An adopted level chest's level GUID, sixteen hex digits as from Stash.levelChests, or '' for any other container.

isStorage.summary: Whether it is a storage with no chest.

locked.summary: Whether it is locked, which stops it opening. Unlocking in the game with a key or lockpick fires stashUnlocked. You can assign to it.

lockStyle.summary: The lock the game's minigame shows, 'common' or 'fancy', as set by a script for all players, or null for the level's. Assign 'common', 'fancy' or null, and anything else throws a RangeError.

lockLevel.summary: How hard the lock is to pick, from 0, easy, to 1, hard, as set by a script for all players. Null means the game's value, either an adopted chest's level value or one the game makes up. Assign 0 to 1, or null.

serverLocked.exampleLua:
if chest.serverLocked then
  print("locked by a script")
end

canBePicked.summary: Whether players can pick its lock. You can assign to it.

isOpen.summary: Whether a player has it open.
isOpen.exampleLua:
if chest.isOpen then
  kcds.core.Chat.sendToPlayer(player, "Someone is going through it.")
end

heldById.summary: The id of the player with it open, or 0.

itemCount.summary: The number of item rows it holds.

getInventory.summary: Its contents as { revision, items }, or null.
getInventory.exampleLua:
local contents = chest:getInventory()
if contents then
  local lines = {}
  for _, row in ipairs(contents.items) do
    table.insert(lines, row.amount .. " " .. row.name)
  end
  print(table.concat(lines, ", "))
end

params.request: { item, amount }, and optional properties such as quality and health.

addItem.exampleLua:
local answer = chest:addItem({ item = "apple", amount = 5 })
if not answer.ok then
  print("not added: " .. tostring(answer.code))
end

params.request: { units: [{ id, amount }], revision?, notify? }, with row ids from getInventory().

removeItem.exampleLua:
local apples = nil
for _, row in ipairs(chest:getInventory().items) do
  if row.name == "apple" then
    apples = row
    break
  end
end
if apples then
  chest:removeItem({ units = { { id = apples.id, amount = 2 } } })
end

setInventory.exampleCs: chest.SetInventory(new { items = new object[] { new { item = "arrow_crude", amount = 50 } } });

open.summary: Opens the stash for a player, returning false if it cannot open.

params.player: The player: anywhere in their dimension for a storage, or within 5 m for a chest. It returns false while another player has it open. Only a player's own use of it shows them the Locales text stash.inUse.

open.exampleLua:
-- A bank opened by a command.
local vault = kcds.world.Stash.createStorage()

kcds.core.Events.on("playerCommand", function(player, command)
  if command == "bank" then
    vault:open(player)
  end
end)

destroy.summary: Removes the stash, firing stashDestroy, and closes it for a player with it open.

guid.summary: Its GUID, sixteen hex digits, or '' for a storage.

keyClass.summary: Which key item class fits its lock, by GUID, or '' if no key does. You can assign to it.

inventoryOf.summary: For a view from Stash.playerInventory, the player whose inventory it shows, otherwise null.
inventoryOf.exampleLua:
kcds.core.Events.on("stashOpen", function(stash, player)
  if stash.inventoryOf then
    print(player.nickname .. " opened " .. stash.inventoryOf.nickname .. "'s inventory")
  end
end)

body.summary: For a searchable body, the player it belongs to, otherwise null.
body.exampleLua:
kcds.core.Events.on("stashOpen", function(stash, player)
  if stash.body then
    kcds.core.Chat.sendToPlayer(stash.body, player.nickname .. " searches you.")
  end
end)
